substances.name: Vitamin D3
substances.citation: pubmed:24885631 — Jones et al. 2014, J Clin Endocrinol Metab
secondary_citations: pubmed:24885631 — Jones et al. 2014, J Clin Endocrinol Metab (25(OH)D2 half-life 13.9 d; DBP-genotype dependence)
substances.params_note: Half-life is of circulating 25(OH)D3, not parent cholecalciferol: 15.1 +/- 3.1 d overall, 14.7 d Gambia vs 15.6 d UK; 25(OH)D2 13.9 +/- 2.6 d; half-life scales with vitamin-D-binding-protein concentration (pubmed:24885631 — Jones et al. 2014, J Clin Endocrinol Metab). Steady state of the 25(OH)D pool takes ~2-3 months of daily dosing.
substances.rationale: D3 acts through the accumulating 25-hydroxylated pool: large distribution volume with DBP sequestration means body status, not a plasma decay curve, tracks effect; the 15-day 25(OH)D3 half-life reflects pool turnover over weeks.

substances.name: Vitamin K2 (MK-7)
secondary_citations: pubmed:17158229 — Schurgers et al. 2007, Blood (MK-7 accumulates 7-8-fold vs MK-4 during prolonged intake)
substances.params_note: MK-7 circulates up to 144 h; 10-fold higher postprandial serum levels than vitamin K1, absorbed within 4 h (pubmed:32575901 — Akbulut et al. 2020, Nutrients); prolonged MK-7 intake drives serum accumulation to 7-8x baseline with much more stable levels than MK-4 (pubmed:17158229 — Schurgers et al. 2007, Blood).
substances.rationale: MK-7 is the canonical accumulating vitamin K: multi-day plasma retention plus documented 7-8-fold serum accumulation on chronic dosing; effect (osteocalcin/MGP carboxylation) is sustained over days rather than tracking a decay limb.

substances.name: Omega-3 fish oil (EPA/DHA)
secondary_citations: pubmed:41956323 — Symington et al. 2026, Am J Clin Nutr (whole-body n-3 PUFA turnover half-lives: EPA 3.4 +/- 2.7 d, n-3 DPA 6.4 +/- 5.3 d, DHA 6.3 +/- 8.9 d)
substances.params_note: Point/range are single-dose plasma half-lives of the acid forms: EPA 45 +/- 8 h, DHA 66 +/- 12 h after 2.2-2.3 g ethyl esters (pubmed:39299684 — Schmieta et al. 2025, Lipids). Tissue (delta-13C traced) half-life is days, not hours: EPA 3.4 d, DHA 6.3 d (pubmed:41956323 — Symington et al. 2026, Am J Clin Nutr).
substances.rationale: Effect (membrane enrichment / omega-3 index) tracks tissue incorporation and phospholipid turnover over days-to-weeks, not the ~2-day plasma decay limb; plasma clearance is fast relative to the slow loading of cell membranes, so model as accumulation with plasma half-lives only as the distribution limb.

substances.name: CoQ10 (ubiquinone-10)
substances.citation: pubmed:3781673 — Tomono et al. 1986, Int J Clin Pharmacol Ther Toxicol
secondary_citations: pubmed:16551570 — Bhagavan & Chopra 2006, Free Radic Res (Tmax ~6 h, elimination half-life about 33 h; tissue/mitochondrial uptake)
substances.params_note: Terminal half-life 33.19 +/- 5.32 h after 100 mg d5-CoQ10 (n=16), Tmax 6.5 h, second plasma peak at 24 h from liver->VLDL redistribution (pubmed:3781673 — Tomono et al. 1986, Int J Clin Pharmacol Ther Toxicol); plasma reference interval 0.40-1.91 umol/L and tissue uptake into heart/brain mitochondria with high dosing (pubmed:16551570 — Bhagavan & Chopra 2006, Free Radic Res).
substances.rationale: Lipoprotein/liver handling and lipophilic tissue loading (biphasic curve, 24-h second peak) mean plasma level is a redistribution proxy while mitochondrial pools load over weeks of dosing — tissue-loading model with steady state over days-weeks, plasma t1/2 noted in params.

substances.name: Curcumin
substances.citation: pubmed:42225688 — Kim et al. 2026, Sci Rep
secondary_citations: pubmed:11712783 — Cheng et al. 2001, Anticancer Res (serum peak 1-2 h, decline within 12 h after dosing up to 8 g/day)
pubmed:9619120 — Shoba et al. 1998, Planta Med (piperine raises curcumin bioavailability 2000%; shortens apparent half-life)
substances.params_note: Terminal t1/2 24.92 h for free curcumin vs 6.74 h for a nano-liposomal formulation; the study itself cautions the long free-curcumin t1/2 is apparent/absorption-linked (pubmed:42225688 — Kim et al. 2026, Sci Rep). Plain curcumin is often undetectable in serum at <=2 g (pubmed:9619120 — Shoba et al. 1998, Planta Med).
substances.rationale: Curve is dominated by slow, poor absorption plus glucuronidation/enterohepatic recycling: Cmax at 1-2 h (Cheng) yet terminal slope of ~25 h is flip-flop-like absorption-controlled decline, not a clean one-compartment elimination; absorption+elimination model required.

substances.name: Quercetin
substances.citation: pubmed:11361045 — Graefe et al. 2001, J Clin Pharmacol
secondary_citations: pubmed:10363620 — Graefe et al. 1999, Int J Clin Pharmacol Ther (IV elimination half-lives 2.4 h and 0.7 h; oral absorption 0->50% of dose)
substances.params_note: Terminal elimination half-life ~11 h for all oral treatments (quercetin measured as plasma glucuronides); Tmax 0.7 h for quercetin-4'-glucoside/onion vs 4.3-7.0 h for rutin/buckwheat — sugar moiety controls rate (pubmed:11361045 — Graefe et al. 2001, J Clin Pharmacol). IV t1/2 only 0.7-2.4 h (pubmed:10363620 — Graefe et al. 1999, Int J Clin Pharmacol Ther).
substances.rationale: Plasma contains virtually only conjugated metabolites, and the oral terminal half-life (~11 h) far exceeds the IV half-life (0.7-2.4 h) — classic absorption/conjugation-controlled (flip-flop-prone) kinetics; absorption+elimination two-limb model is mandatory.

substances.name: Apigenin
substances.params_note: Cited oral T1/2 average 2.52 +/- 0.56 h, reported range 1.8-4.2 h, Tmax 0.5-2.5 h, oral bioavailability ~30%; note the half-life estimates in that review derive from rodent PK studies (Wan 2007; Chen 2003) — human half-life not directly established (pubmed:34084146 — DeRango-Adem & Blay 2021, Front Pharmacol).
substances.rationale: No primary human elimination study; modeled as a short half-life absorption-limited flavone from review-compiled data, with enteroheptic biliary recycling prolonging mucosal exposure; treat the half-life as provisional and rodent-derived.

substances.name: Resveratrol
substances.citation: pubmed:15333514 — Walle et al. 2004, Drug Metab Dispos
substances.params_note: Plasma half-life 9.2 +/- 0.6 h refers to total radioactivity (resveratrol + metabolites) after a 25-mg oral 14C dose; parent resveratrol stayed <5 ng/mL; absorption >=70% with peak total levels 491 +/- 90 ng/mL (pubmed:15333514 — Walle et al. 2004, Drug Metab Dispos).
substances.rationale: >=70% absorbed but almost entirely sulfate/glucuronide-hydrogenated metabolites in plasma — the measured 9.2 h limb is metabolite disposition after very rapid intestinal first-pass, so a plain one-compartment decay on parent drug is invalid; absorption+metabolite model needed.

substances.name: Phosphatidylserine
substances.rationale: Documented non-verdict for a one-compartment curve: dietary/supplemental PS is hydrolyzed in the gut to lysophospholipid/base before absorption and reassembled into host phospholipid pools; there is no established, citable human plasma elimination half-life for oral PS, and circulating PS effect is structural/membrane-based rather than a plasma concentration curve. Parameterizing 'PS plasma t1/2' would be invented.
